loop_22mhz.observable: Mean brightness-temperature excess above a local background over selected spur pixels; K. The paper selects loop pixels between the Table 1 lower and upper absolute-temperature contours, subtracts surrounding background, and reports Table 2 averages. Spectral beta fits 22, 408, 820, and 1420 MHz with T proportional to frequency^-beta.
loop_22mhz.distance: Not assigned by this paper's brightness table; any three-dimensional shell distance is a separate, model-dependent input.
loop_22mhz.conditioning_status: partial: lowsky references this paper for low-frequency loop indices and uses related 408-MHz/loop priors; 22-MHz amplitudes are useful comparison data, not a blind holdout for every loop.
loop_22mhz.caveat: The authors specifically caution that Loop IV has a large assumed background and may have an underestimated 22-MHz excess. Their contour boundaries and background estimates are part of the measurement, so a model should be measured with the same aperture/background rule.

gum_low_frequency.region: 240 < Galactic longitude < 280 deg; -15 < Galactic latitude < 15 deg
gum_low_frequency.selection_and_calibration: Comparison of 3.93-MHz RAE-1 and 4.7-MHz ground survey brightness with an extrapolation of 30-150 MHz diffuse continuum; the latter requires component separation from SNRs and background.
gum_low_frequency.conditioning_status: conditioned: lowsky explicitly uses the historical roughly threefold Gum depression
gum_low_frequency.caveat: The ratio is approximate prose, not a tabulated data point. The paper calls tau_4 < 3 +/- 1 an upper limit and its 1300 pc cm^-6 EM and hot electron-temperature interpretation are historical model-dependent values, not independent modern measurements.

orion_eridanus_halpha.source: Pon et al. (2014), MNRAS 441, 1095, sections 1 and 2.1
orion_eridanus_halpha.region: Eridanus filaments (Arcs A, B, C) versus adjacent superbubble wall
orion_eridanus_halpha.conditioning_status: conditioned: lowsky cites this paper for Orion geometry and H-alpha brightness priors
orion_eridanus_halpha.caveat: The paper's intensities are prose-order-of-magnitude descriptions, without tabulated statistical errors. Converting H-alpha to EM assumes temperature, dust extinction, and line-of-sight geometry; these should not be treated as independent radio absorption data.

gum_purcell_shell.source: Purcell et al. (2015), ApJ 804, 22, abstract and fitted model
gum_purcell_shell.fit_region: Relatively clean upper Gum Nebula; lower/plane region confused
gum_purcell_shell.conditioning_status: conditioned: explicit Gum geometry/density/filling priors in lowsky
gum_purcell_shell.caveat: These are correlated parameters from an RM plus H-alpha spherical-shell fit, not direct EM measurements, and the warm-gas volume filling factor is not a two-dimensional radio beam covering fraction.
